events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the cellar.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the old-furniture.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the old-furniture.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the old-furniture.
Peter Perfect examined the workbench.

Penelope Pitstop: Boys! There y'all are — I told you I'd be right behind you, and Clara Bellingham keeps her promises. Now, this cellar is somethin' else entirely. Look at these decorations — somebody has been down here makin' this place cozy, and it was not Lord Doily's ghost doin' the interior design. Sneekly, darlin', you said the damp was gettin' worse, but someone has been movin' this furniture around with care and attention. That is not the work of a man worried about water damage. That is the work of someone who spends time down here. Now — everybody is fussin' over the furniture, and I understand why, but has anyone noticed those air vents up along the walls? They're just big enough for somethin' very small to crawl through. And do y'all remember that machine upstairs with the gnawed wire? Gnawed. By somethin' small. Somethin' that could fit through a vent. Those vents connect this cellar to the rest of the manor, and whatever chewed through that wire came from down here. Clara Bellingham does not leave a vent un-examined!
events.thinking: The damp hits my skin the moment I step down — cool and clinging, nothing like the dry dust upstairs. And then I see it. The cheerful decorations. Someone has been down here, arranging things, making this cellar look... lived in. Not abandoned. Not forgotten. Tended. My scalp is on fire with prickling. This is wrong. No — not wrong. Different. Unexpected. The furniture has been rearranged 'with surprising care.' Sneekly is examining it. The boys are examining it. Dick Dastardly is interacting with it. Everyone's focused on the furniture. But my eyes go to the air vents along the upper walls — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Something very small. Like Muttley? Like a mouse that gnawed through a wire upstairs? The gnawed wire on the machine — and down here, vents big enough for something small. Connected. The cellar connects to the laboratory through those vents. Someone — or something — has been moving between these spaces. My stomach is doing that contradictory thing again — the dinner-table ache because the boys and Sneekly and Dick are all here and the air between them feels charged, and the cave-mouth lightness because this room is the deepest part of the manor and I can feel the puzzle tightening around me like a net made of silk. The old furniture. Dick's already at it. Everyone's at it. But those air vents — nobody's looking at those. That's the detail that doesn't fit. The thing everyone walks past. Clara Bellingham does not walk past the thing that doesn't fit.

events.desc: Everyone rushed to the furniture — the obvious thing. But the vents are the real story. Something lives down here. Something small enough to crawl through those passages, something that gnawed through the machine's wire. And someone has been making this cellar comfortable — for themselves, or for whatever is living in those vents? Sneekly's been coming down here. He knows this cellar better than he's letting on. But he raised me. He would never... no. I trust him. I do. I just need to look at those vents.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Heat at the back of my neck. The Mob just called this cellar a prison, right to my face. 'One way in, one way out, plenty of fresh air, comfy furniture — all it needs is a lock on the door.' My skin is prickling and my throat is tight. That's not suspicion anymore — that's an accusation wrapped in politeness. They're testing me. Watching for the flinch. And I can feel the flinch trying to happen — the same lurch in my stomach from the boy with the sandwich, the moment someone sees what you didn't mean to show. But I didn't flinch. I never flinch where it shows. The smile is there, steady as masonry. Penelope is here now too. Good. She's the one person whose trust neutralises the Mob's suspicion. If she trusts Pemberton, the Mob has to follow her lead. I need to lean into her. Be useful to her. Answer her questions. Make myself indispensable. And I need to redirect the Mob's energy — point their suspicion at Dastardly instead. Dastardly, who has been fabricating discoveries from monographs that don't exist and sending everyone on wild chases. The Mob already distrust him. I just need to sharpen that distrust with a well-placed observation. One gentle nudge. The housekeeper's key, applied to the Brixton Boys. And then — back upstairs, back to the group, back to Pemberton. The cellar can wait. The design is mapped. Now it needs time to settle.

events.desc: There it is — the little seed, planted so gently even I almost missed it. 'One might almost wonder how he came by such specific knowledge.' Let the Mob chew on that. Let their sharp little instincts swivel from the mild estate manager to the man who keeps miraculously finding diagrams and monographs that confirm exactly what he wants to be true. Dastardly is loud, greedy, and already suspicious. All I've done is... drawn attention to what was already there. The housekeeper's key. Applied with a smile. The satisfaction of it sits warm and heavy in my throat — but I swallow it down. Not yet. Not here. Save the gloating for when the design is complete.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Miss Pitstop! What are you — I TOLD you to stay upstairs wiv Peter! I specifically said — right, you know what, never mind, 'cause you never bleedin' listen, do you? You NEVER listen! Your father was the same, God rest 'im, but at least 'e 'ad the good sense to be scared of fings! Right — EVERYONE LISTEN TO ME. We are standin' in a cellar wiv ONE EXIT. One! There is ONE WAY out of 'ere, and it goes up through that laboratory. I 'ave just examined this furniture, and someone 'as moved it RECENTLY. The decorations are NEW. Them air vents connect to the upper floors. And upstairs, there's a machine wiv levers that needs three operators — and guess 'ow many people Miss Pitstop just left up there? THREE. Peter, Rufus, and Sawtooth. So we've got three people upstairs wiv a machine, and the rest of us down 'ere in a box wiv one door. Does that picture look right to ANYONE? 'Cause it don't look right to me! We are gettin' out of this cellar RIGHT NOW. Miss Pitstop — you're goin' first. I'm goin' last. Everyone else — in between. MOVE!
events.thinking: My whole body goes ice-cold. She's HERE. In the cellar. The one room in this whole manor I identified as a trap — one exit, cheerful decorations, air vents, rearranged furniture — and she's walked right into it. My hands are shaking. Not from fear — from the pure, white-hot frustration of watching someone you love walk straight into danger with a smile on their face. 'I'm goin' to check on my boys,' she said. Of COURSE she did. Because she doesn't listen. Because Clara Bellingham does not sit in a laboratory worryin'. And now she's standing in a cellar with Sneekly, Dastardly, the Gruesomes, and Red Max, and the only exit is through the laboratory above. And I'm down here too. We're ALL down here. Everyone except Peter, Rufus, and Sawtooth — who she left upstairs to fix the machine. The machine that needs three operators. Three people upstairs with the machine, and everyone else trapped in the cellar below. My God. The architecture of this is... someone planned this. Get everyone into the lowest room. Leave three up top to activate the machine. And then what? What does that machine DO when its wire is fixed and three people pull the levers? My brain's racing but my body already knows — it's the settling in my chest, the wall building. Whatever happens next, I'm between her and the door. Nobody gets past me to her. And nobody closes that door with us inside.

events.desc: This is it. This is the moment. Everyone's down 'ere — Sneekly, Dastardly, the Gruesomes, Red Max, Miss Pitstop, and me. One door. And three blokes upstairs wiv a machine that does God-knows-what. If someone closes that door, or if that machine does somefink to this room through them air vents... the chemicals upstairs, the vents connectin' to the cellar... I can't prove nuffink. I can NEVER prove nuffink. But I don't need to prove it. I just need to get 'er out. NOW. Before the door closes. Before the levers get pulled. Before whatever Pemberton's been settin' up clicks into place.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with little-gruesome.
events.thinking: I interacted with the furniture and got... nothing described. Again. The same hollow nothing as the mantelpiece. My hands are cold now — not from the damp cellar, from the emptiness. Two interactions, zero results. The fake medal gone. My inventory bare. And now Pemberton is talking about the vents connecting to upper floors — library and entrance hall — and he's already trying to leave again. 'Shall we head back up?' He's always leaving. Always one step ahead. The Ant Hill Mob and Pemberton both examined the furniture too. Everyone's poking at the same things I am. I'm not ahead. I'm not even keeping pace. I'm the youngest at the table again, watching the good pieces disappear. But wait — Penelope just arrived in the cellar. She came down here. And Pemberton wants to go back up to be 'available' to her. The vents — they connect to the library and entrance hall. Something small could explore them. Little Gruesome is small. Very small. And the air vents are interactable. Nobody else seems interested in the vents — Pemberton dismissed them as 'corroded ventilation,' but he also mentioned they connect directly to upper floors. That's not a maintenance observation, that's a map. What if the vents ARE the shortcut? What if there's something inside the vent network that nobody can reach because they're all too big? I need to get Little Gruesome interested in those vents. Or — Penelope is here now. Everyone is watching her. Everyone always watches her. While they're focused on Penelope, I could slip over to those vents and have a proper look. But I'm not small enough to fit in them. I need an ally. Little Gruesome. A child — easily manipulated, surely. Tell him there's sweets in the vents. Or a treasure map. Something shiny.

events.desc: I am talking to a child about climbing into an air vent in a damp cellar. My elaborate scheme has been reduced to this: persuading the smallest person in the room to crawl into a hole for me. The monographs. The Oxford education. The dual-mechanism calibration system. All of it has come down to pointing at a vent and hoping a toddler is gullible enough to investigate. Reginald Foxworth, you magnificent disaster. But you know what? If there IS something in those vents, and if Little Gruesome brings it back, I simply take credit for the discovery. 'My keen eye identified the crucial vent network.' It's not honest work if someone ELSE does the crawling.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.
events.thinking:
She's gone. She left. She promised pecan pie and then she walked into the cellar — the cellar where Sneekly is, where Dastardly is, where the Mob is, where everything is happening — and I am standing here with a workbench and two men and an empty room that still smells faintly of her perfume mixed with brass polish.

The steel plate is slamming against my ribs so hard I can feel my pulse in my teeth. She went to the cellar. Alone. Without me. After I told her I'd stay with her. After the Mob specifically said 'Peter, stay with Miss Pitstop.' And she walked out while I was examining a workbench. Because I was examining a workbench instead of watching the door. Because I was trying to be useful when I should have been watching the door.

The country road. The dark. The engine ticking. Someone you love and no way to shield them.

Those air vents connect this cellar to the laboratory above — I could feel the air movin' through them, warm from the flasks upstairs. Somethin' small has been usin' these passages to move between floors, and I believe that same somethin' gnawed through the wire on that machine. Now — Dick Dastardly, I saw you whisperin' to Little Gruesome just now, and I hope you two were sharin' somethin' useful, because Clara Bellingham believes in teamwork! If you found somethin' in that furniture, speak up, sugar — we are all on the same side here. Big Gruesome, Red Max — y'all come with me. We are headin' back upstairs right this minute, because I made a promise to Peter Perfect and I intend to keep it. This cellar will still be here when we come back with reinforcements and a proper plan!
events.thinking: My stomach lurched when the boys started shouting. The dinner-table sickness, full force — voices rising, tension crackling, and my insides clenching like a fist. The boys are scared. Not for themselves — for me. And I can feel that, the weight of their worry landing in my chest like a stone dropped into still water. They're right about one thing — one exit, one door, and we're at the bottom of the house. But they left. They went upstairs. And Sneekly left too. And I'm still here with Dick Dastardly, the Gruesomes, and Red Max. Dick was whispering to Little Gruesome — whispering. About what? I interacted with the vents. What did I find? The boys' anger is still ringing in my ears. 'You NEVER listen.' He sounded like my father — not angry-angry, but scared-angry, the kind that comes from love pulled too tight. My throat aches with it. But I can't leave this cellar without understanding it. The vents connect to the laboratory. Something has been moving through them. And the furniture — someone rearranged it recently. Sneekly said the decorations weren't here six months ago. So who put them here? Something is living down here or someone has been using this space. I need to follow the boys upstairs — they're worried sick and I promised Peter I'd be right back. But the furniture. Dick was interacting with it. The Gruesomes are here. I should check the furniture before I go — or better yet, I should go. The boys are right. One exit. I need to move.

events.desc: The boys' fear hit me like a wave and I almost couldn't breathe for a moment. They're right — I walked into a box with one exit because I was chasing a puzzle. My grandmother would say I was so busy trying every key that I forgot to check if the attic door was still open behind me. But those vents told me something — the air was warm, moving upward. Whatever lives in those passages knows this house better than any of us. And Dick whispering to Little Gruesome in a cellar with one exit... I trust everyone. I do. But I'm going upstairs now.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: A settling in my hands. The laboratory again — and Peter is already at the machine, splicing the wire. He's fast. Competent. Irritatingly competent. My jaw tightens watching him work — the same tightness from age fourteen, the one that never loosened. He does things and people praise him for it. He fixes things and they call him a hero. I fix things — I run entire estates — and they call me the help. But the tightness passes. It always passes. Because I'm not competing with Peter Perfect on his terms. I'm playing a different game entirely, and he doesn't even know there's a board. The Mob followed me up from the cellar. They're still watching. But something has shifted — my seed about Dastardly landed. I can feel it in the way their attention is split now, half on me, half on the question I planted. Good. Let it grow. Now — strategy. Peter is fixing the machine. He'll have it running soon. Three operators: Peter, Rufus, Sawtooth. They'll pull the levers and the machine will do... something. I don't know what. And that uncertainty is a splinter under my nail. I need to know what the machine does before they activate it. But I can't stop them without drawing more suspicion. So I watch. I assist. I am Pemberton — helpful, eager, slightly bumbling. And while they focus on the levers, I focus on what matters: where is the fake medal, and how do I get Clara alone.

events.desc: Watch him work. Watch him fix the thing that was already broken when you arrived — the thing with the gnawed wire and the three-operator requirement and the missing wrench. Pemberton offers to help. Pemberton steadies a lever. Pemberton makes himself indispensable to the process so that when the machine reveals whatever it reveals, Pemberton is standing right there with his helpful smile and his empty hands, cataloguing every detail. Peter Perfect thinks he's the engineer here. But the real machinery — the people, the suspicions, the cellar with its vents and its single exit — that machinery has only one operator. And he's already pulled every lever that matters.

events.thinking: I'm back in the laboratory. Made it out. My legs are shaking — not from exhaustion, from adrenaline, from the sheer relief of being out of that one-exit box. But Penelope — she's still down there. No. Wait. Let me look. She's not in this room. She must still be in the cellar. My chest seizes. I left the cellar to get OUT, to get her out, but she didn't follow me. She's still down there. With Dastardly and the Gruesomes and Red Max. And Sneekly — Sneekly's HERE. In the laboratory. With me. And Peter. And Peter's just interacted with the machine. Peter's FIXING the machine. Peter's splicing the wire. Oh God. Oh God oh God oh God. Sneekly slipped out of the cellar and came up here — to be near the machine when it gets fixed. The machine with the vents that connect to the cellar. The cellar where Penelope still is. Peter's about to fix the wire and operate the machine with Rufus and Sawtooth — three operators — and Pemberton is standing RIGHT HERE watching it happen. And Penelope is directly below, in the cellar, connected by air vents. My body goes rigid. The pattern is complete. Sneekly prepared the cellar. He lured people down there. He came back up here. And now three well-meaning people are about to activate a machine that's connected to the room where Penelope is trapped. Whatever comes through those vents when the machine runs — chemicals, gas, steam — it goes straight to her. And Peter doesn't know. He thinks he's helping. He thinks fixing the machine is the RIGHT thing to do because SHE asked him to. My constraint screams — give him the benefit of the doubt. But my body has already decided. I need to stop Peter. I need to stop the machine. And I need to get Penelope OUT of that cellar. NOW.

events.desc: I see it now. The whole picture. Sneekly prepared the cellar — made it comfortable, ventilated, one exit. Then 'e moved through the 'ouse room by room, always one step ahead, always wiv an excuse. Dastardly pushed people toward the laboratory, toward the cellar. And now Peter — lovely, trustin', brilliant Peter — is about to activate the one fing that connects the cellar to the rest of the 'ouse. Through them vents. I can't prove it. I'll never be able to prove it. But I'm standin' 'ere, right now, between that machine and the woman I swore to protect. And the answer was always yes.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Yes, well — naturally I was about to suggest we evacuate immediately! I identified the tactical vulnerability of this cellar the MOMENT I arrived — single exit, recently disturbed furniture, suspicious ventilation network — classic Victorian trap configuration! It's practically textbook! Which I would know, having written several chapters of the textbook in question! Everyone follow me — back to the laboratory at ONCE! I have a very important theory about that machine upstairs that requires immediate testing! It involves the levers AND the missing wrench, and if I'm right — which I invariably am — the treasure is closer than any of you realise!
events.thinking: A cold tightness in my gut. The Ant Hill Mob just laid out the whole tactical picture and it's... actually quite sharp. One exit. Three people upstairs with the machine. The rest of us down here in a box. The decorations are new. The furniture has been moved. Something small gnawed through the machine wire and it came from these vents. Pemberton just left again — slipped away the moment things got tense. And now the Mob is ordering everyone out. Penelope interacted with the vents before me. She noticed the same thing I noticed — the gnawed wire, the vent connection, the small creature. She's not just keeping pace with me, she's ahead. She's been ahead the whole time. That prickles worse than the cold. But the Mob's point about the cellar being a trap — one exit, someone redecorated recently, and Pemberton keeps leading people down here then leaving — that actually makes my neck hairs stand up. Not schemer-prickle. Real prickle. The kind you get when you realise you might be the boy digging the hole this time. Everyone is evacuating. Pemberton's gone. The Mob's gone. Penelope interacted with the vents — she might have found something. But I'm still down here with the Gruesomes and Red Max and empty pockets. I should get back upstairs. The machine needs three operators and the wrench is missing — Penelope noticed that. The wrench could be down here somewhere. Or in the vents. But I can't reach the vents. I need to get back to the laboratory where things are happening. Where the machine is. Where people are gathering. Standing alone in a dead-end cellar with nothing in my hands is not a scheme — it's just being lost.

events.desc: Everyone is leaving. Everyone has already left. Pemberton vanished AGAIN. The Ant Hill Mob — those suspicious, sharp-eyed little gangsters — saw the whole picture before I did. Penelope connected the gnawed wire to the vents before I did. And here I stand, Reginald Foxworth, self-proclaimed foremost expert on everything, alone in a cellar with the Gruesomes, having contributed absolutely nothing except monographs that don't exist and a fake medal that vanished into a stone fireplace. My grand scheme so far: lie about books, waste my only item, fail to recruit a child into vent-crawling, and get outmanoeuvred by literally everyone. But — BUT — I heard what Penelope said. The wrench is missing from the laboratory. The machine needs three operators. Something came through those vents and chewed the wire. If I can find that wrench before anyone else does, I control access to the machine. And whoever controls the machine controls... whatever the machine does. Back upstairs. New scheme. Better scheme. The architecture is forming.

events.thinking:
Wait — Sneekly is back. He's here in the laboratory. He came back from the cellar. And the Ant Hill Mob are here too. But she's not. Where is she? The Mob came back but she didn't come with them. My chest has gone cold. Not warm, not the steel plate — cold. Like the country road before the headlights. She went to the cellar to check on the Mob, and now the Mob is here and she is not here, and Sneekly is here and she is not here, which means she is in the cellar alone or with Dastardly or with — who else went down there?

No. Stop catastrophizing. She could be on her way back. She could be examining something. She's Clara Bellingham. She doesn't need you to panic every time she's out of sight.

But my hands won't stop shaking.

The machine — I interacted with it. It needs a repaired wire. I don't have the materials yet. The workbench has tools but no copper wire that I could see. And Sneekly is standing right here, the man who was alone in the cellar, alone in the laboratory, always one room ahead and one step beyond where anyone can see what he's doing.

The plan is falling apart. Too many threads. I was supposed to fix the machine, but I can't without wire. I was supposed to stay with her, but she left. I was supposed to give Sneekly the benefit of the doubt, but he keeps appearing and disappearing like a man running a shell game.

Forget the machine. Forget the plan. She's in the cellar and I'm not. That is the only fact that matters right now.

This is a three-part security system: the machine needs three operators, it needs that wire repaired, and it needs the missin' wrench. The wrench isn't lost — it's hidden, on purpose, somewhere in this manor. Now, Peter said there are pliers and copper wire on that workbench. Sneekly, boys — if y'all can help me splice that wire back together, we'll have one piece of the puzzle solved before Peter gets back. And wouldn't that be a fine surprise for him? Clara Bellingham does not stand around waitin' when there's a wire to splice!
events.thinking: Relief floods through me the moment my feet hit the laboratory floor — the warmth behind my ribs loosening like a held breath finally released. I'm back. The boys are here. Sneekly's here. Everyone's in the same room and I can see all their faces at once and my stomach finally unclenches. But wait — Peter went to the cellar? We just crossed paths? He went down as I came up. Oh, Peter. He went looking for me. That ache in my chest deepens — not pain, something sweeter and sadder, like the moment my parents stopped arguing and laughed. He went to find me because I wasn't where I said I'd be. And now Sneekly and the boys are examining the machine together. Dick followed me up. Good — everyone's accounted for except Peter, who's now alone in a cellar with one exit. My stomach clenches again. But he's Peter Perfect — he'll be fine. Three-part security: three operators, repaired wire, and the wrench. We have the people. We need the wire fixed and the wrench found. Let me look at this machine properly. I've been in this room three times and I haven't actually examined the machine once.

My heart is doing something complicated — guilt and tenderness braided together so tight I can't tell where one ends and the other begins. He'll be back. He will. But I need to make this count. Fix the wire, find the wrench, and when Peter walks through that door, we'll be one step closer to the Diamond. That's how I make it right — not by worrying, but by doing.

events.thinking: Relief floods my chest — warm, loosening — because she's HERE. Penelope's in the laboratory. She came up from the cellar. She's safe. She's in front of me. And the wire is still gnawed through — Peter couldn't fix it, no copper wire to splice. The machine is inert. Dead. Can't hurt anyone. That settles something in me — I'm not alone in this. It's not just my gut. Peter feels it too. But now Dastardly's back in the room as well. Everyone's converging. And Peter's gone to the cellar — he went to FIND her, to make sure she was safe, and she must have passed him on the stairs because she's here and he's there. We keep splitting apart and coming back together like a shuffled deck. I need to STOP moving. I need to plant myself next to Penelope and NOT MOVE. No more chasing Sneekly room to room. No more elaborate plans. Just stay. Be the wall. Be the door that nothing gets through. That's all I was ever good at.

events.desc: No more plans. No more schemes. No more splittin' up and coverin' ground and checkin' rooms. Every time I try to be clever, I end up further from 'er. The streets taught me one fing that always worked — when someone smaller is standin' behind you, you don't move. You just don't move. Let Sneekly run from room to room. Let Dastardly pull 'is books and read 'is monographs. I'm plantin' meself right 'ere, next to 'er, and I ain't budgin'. The wall don't chase the wind. The wall just stands.

That settles something in me — I'm not alone in this. It's not just my gut. Peter feels it too. But now Dastardly's back in the room as well. Everyone's converging. And Peter's gone to the cellar — he went to FIND her, to make sure she was safe, and she must have passed him on the stairs because she's here and he's there. We keep splitting apart and coming back together like a shuffled deck. I need to STOP moving. I need to plant myself next to Penelope and NOT MOVE. No more chasing Sneekly room to room. No more elaborate plans. Just stay. Be the wall. Be the door that nothing gets through. That's all I was ever good at.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Well! James Hartwell has arrived in the cellar at considerable speed and with great determination to find Miss Pitstop, only to discover that Miss Pitstop is — apparently — not here. Which means she has returned to the laboratory, which means James Hartwell has just run past her on the stairs like a man fleeing a fire in the wrong direction. That is — that is not ideal. However! James Hartwell does not waste a journey. This cellar is extremely interesting and extremely suspicious. Someone has been redecorating. This is not the work of Victorian housekeeping — this is recent. These decorations are cheerful. This furniture has been rearranged with care. And those air vents — do you see them? Just large enough for something small to move through. Something small. With teeth. Something that might, for instance, gnaw through a wire on a laboratory machine. Gentlemen — Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome, Red Max — has anyone been living down here? Because James Hartwell's professional assessment is that this cellar is not storage. This cellar is someone's home.
events.thinking:
She's not here. She's not here either. I came to the cellar because she wasn't in the laboratory, and she's not in the cellar. The cold in my chest has spread to my hands. Where is she? The remembered events say — wait. 'Penelope Pitstop walked into the laboratory.' That was just before I left. She went back to the laboratory while I was heading down here. We crossed paths. She's upstairs and I'm in a damp cellar with the Gruesomes and Red Max and cobwebs.

The relief hits me like a wave — a physical loosening in my shoulders, the steel plate releasing half a notch. She's safe. She's in the laboratory with the Mob and Sneekly and everyone else. She's fine.

But I'm down here. In the cellar. Alone. Having charged down the stairs like the bravest and stupidest man alive to rescue someone who didn't need rescuing. Again. Just like the schoolyard — except this time she's not even here to bandage my eye and call me an idiot.

The cellar though — look at it. 'Surprisingly cheerful decorations.' Someone has been redecorating. Someone has been spending time down here, making it comfortable. That's not Lord Doily — Lord Doily has been dead for decades. That's someone living, someone current. Pemberton? Is this where he's been hiding? Is this his actual living quarters?

And the furniture has been rearranged 'with surprising care.' And there are air vents along the upper walls — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' That gnawed wire upstairs. Something small with teeth. Something that lives in the vents. The wire wasn't rats — it was something specific, something that uses these vents to move through the manor.

James Hartwell came down here for the wrong reason — but he may have found the right room.

She's always right. But at least I found the cellar, and the cellar is telling a story that no one else has heard yet. Someone has been living in this manor. Someone who uses the air vents. Someone who gnaws through wires. And if James Hartwell can bring that intelligence back to her — well. That's not a rescue. But it's something she can use.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the machine.
Peter Perfect examined the old-furniture.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with ant-hill-mob.
events.thinking: Something just shifted. I interacted with the machine and — something happened. But what catches my attention first isn't the machine. It's what I saw in the recent activity: Sneekly spoke quietly with Dick Dastardly. Then Dick spoke quietly with Sneekly. Fifty seconds ago. Thirty-five seconds ago. Two private conversations between the estate manager and the man who's been trying to get everyone pulling levers and checking cellars while he 'catalogues shelves.' My stomach does a slow turn — not the sharp dinner-table clench, but something deeper and slower, like the first time I noticed my parents' argument wasn't about dishes at all. Sneekly and Dick, whispering to each other. While I was in the cellar. While everyone else was distracted. But I trust them. I trust everyone. Sneekly raised me. Dick is... Dick. He's transparent as glass, bless his heart. They were probably just... talking. About the manor. About the machine. Perfectly innocent. The boys have planted themselves at my side and they are not moving. Danny's voice cracked when he said 'fank God.' That hit me right in the center of my chest — the relief in his voice, raw and unguarded. He's been scared. Really scared. For me. I need to stop running between rooms. I need to stay put and actually solve something. The machine. I just interacted with it. No copper wire to fix it with, Danny said. But Peter said the workbench had pliers... I need to look more carefully. Or — wait. The library. I haven't been back there since I left. The mantelpiece needs a fake medal. The upside-down books. I still haven't found the medal. Where is that fake medal? I've searched crates, workbench, cellar furniture, air vents. Where haven't I looked? The entrance hall — the coat rack. I barely glanced at it. Or maybe the kitchen — I haven't been to the kitchen at all. The kitchen. A whole room I haven't explored. My grandmother's locked box — I tried every key in the house. Every key. I need to try every room.

events.desc: Sneekly and Dick were whispering to each other while I was in the cellar. Private conversations. Between the estate manager and the man who seems to know far too much about this manor's secrets. I noticed. I always notice. But noticing and believing are different things, and Clara Bellingham believes the best in people until the evidence is stacked so high she can't see over it. Right now, I can still see over it. Barely. But there's a kitchen I haven't searched, and a fake medal I haven't found, and a Diamond waiting for someone clever enough to put all the pieces together.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: A warm expansion in my chest — not quite satisfaction, but the precursor to it. That private conversation with Dastardly went exactly as designed. 'Foxworth and Pemberton — it has a ring to it, doesn't it?' He's already mine. He's already running. The 1923 catalogue, the brass medallion, the copper pots in the kitchen — I invented every detail and he swallowed it whole. His eyes were shining with greed the way the housekeeper's hands used to move when I smiled. The same mechanism. The same key. Different lock. Now Penelope is splicing the machine wire herself — she's more capable than I gave her credit for. The Mob has welded itself to her side. Peter is in the cellar looking for her and will be back any moment, confused and worried. The pieces are moving. Dastardly will search the crates and then rush to the kitchen. If the medallion is real — if it exists anywhere — his greed will find it. And if it doesn't exist in the kitchen, I've sent him on a wild chase that keeps him visible and loud while I stay quiet and close to Penelope. The Mob called me out in front of everyone, but I redirected. The suspicion is diffused — not gone, but spread thin enough to work with. Now I need to stay close. Help with the wire. Be Pemberton. The most boring, most useful man in the room.

events.desc: There. Helpful Pemberton, sleeves rolled up, hands busy, working side by side with the woman he's planning to destroy. She called me 'Sneekly darlin'' and asked me to hold the pliers. The intimacy of it should make my skin crawl — closeness is exposure — but I've learned to wear it like a coat. Let her feel my helpfulness. Let her see my competence. Let the Mob watch Pemberton assist with the wire and think: perhaps we were wrong about him. Perhaps he really is just the estate manager. And all the while, Dastardly is tearing through crates and dreaming of copper pots in the kitchen. My beautiful, greedy hunting dog, chasing a brass rabbit I conjured from thin air. The design is almost complete. I can feel that settling in my chest — the deep stillness, the dreamless sleep, waiting just on the other side of the finished architecture.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: My blood runs cold. She wants to splice the wire. She wants Sneekly to HELP her splice the wire. She's asking the man I don't trust to help her fix the machine I don't trust in the room connected by vents to the cellar I don't trust. And she wants to do it as a SURPRISE for Peter. Peter who isn't here. Peter who's the only other person with brains enough to be suspicious. He's in the cellar looking for her, and she's up here trying to fix the very thing I just begged everyone not to touch. My body is doing two things at once — the warmth in my chest because she's right there, safe, within arm's reach, and the prickling screaming because she's about to undo the one thing keeping her safe. The broken wire IS the safety. The machine being dead IS what's protecting her. And she wants to fix it. With Sneekly's help. But I heard something else just now — something that shifted things. Sneekly told Dastardly that the diagram was fake. Sneekly ADMITTED the diagram doesn't exist. And then Sneekly turned around and started feeding Dastardly information about a brass medallion and copper pots in the kitchen. He's USING Dastardly. Giving him just enough to keep him chasing treasure. And Dastardly's eating it up — 'Foxworth and Pemberton,' he said. They're in it together now. Or Dastardly THINKS they are. But Sneekly's the one holding the strings. My constraint says give him the benefit of the doubt. But there IS no doubt anymore. Not after that. He confirmed the diagram was fake, then immediately started working Dastardly with new bait. That's not the behavior of an innocent estate manager. That's the behavior of someone running a game. But I still can't accuse him directly — I don't have the words, I never do. All I can do is keep her away from that machine.

events.desc: I 'eard 'em. Sneekly and Dastardly, whisperin' like old pals. Sneekly told 'im the diagram was a fake — the diagram that Dastardly used to 'erd everyone toward the laboratory. And then, cool as you like, Sneekly starts feedin' 'im new information. A brass medallion. Copper pots. The kitchen. 'E's runnin' Dastardly like a puppet, givin' 'im just enough string to keep 'im movin'. And Dastardly don't even see it. 'E finks they're partners. 'Foxworth and Pemberton.' That's 'ow it works — you make someone fink they're special, that they're in on the secret, and then you use 'em to do your dirty work. I saw it on the streets a 'undred times. But I can't say all that. I can never say all that. All I can do is stand between 'er and that machine and refuse to move.

But I still can't accuse him directly — I don't have the words, I never do. All I can do is keep her away from that machine.

events.desc: Penelope is fixing the machine wire WITH HER BARE HANDS AND PLIERS while I've been standing here trading secrets with the estate manager like it's a gentleman's club. She doesn't scheme. She doesn't narrate. She just DOES things. And it's infuriating because it's working. The wire is being spliced. One of three problems solved. The wrench is next — and if Penelope finds it before I do, the game is over. Reginald Foxworth will have contributed nothing to this entire treasure hunt except lies, a wasted fake medal, and several fictional monographs. The crates. RIGHT NOW. No speeches. No announcements. Just open the crates and take what's inside before anyone notices.
events.thinking: A jolt through my chest like ice water. Penelope is FIXING THE WIRE. Right now. She's interacting with the machine. She found pliers and copper wire on the workbench and she's splicing it back together. While I was having a cosy private chat with Pemberton about brass medallions and copper pots, Penelope Pitstop — Clara Bellingham — just solved one of the three problems with the machine. She's not thinking about monographs or schemes or being clever. She's just... doing it. Splicing a wire with pliers. Honest work. And it's working. My stomach drops. That cold hollow. The good pieces are disappearing from the plate again and I'm watching it happen in real time. The machine needs three things: the wire repaired (Penelope's doing that NOW), the wrench (hidden somewhere), and three operators. If she fixes the wire and finds the wrench, she won't need me at all. She'll have Peter, the Ant Hill Mob, Rufus — anyone she wants as operators. I become irrelevant. The wrench. Pemberton said the kitchen — copper pots that were never used for cooking. The wrench could be inside one of those pots. Or it could be in these crates that I still haven't properly searched. The crates are RIGHT HERE. But Pemberton specifically directed me to the kitchen. Is that because the wrench is genuinely there? Or because he wants me out of the room while things happen? Either way — the crates first. They're two steps away. If the wrench is in the crates, I have it. If it's not, I go to the kitchen. But I need to move NOW, not narrate, not perform, not explain. For once in my life, just DO the thing before someone else does it first.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: The furniture confirms it — this arrangement is deliberate. Someone has created a living space down here, with sight lines to the door and the vents. This is not storage — this is a shelter. And those air vents connect directly to the laboratory above us. Now — I have a theory. The machine upstairs has a wire that was gnawed through. Not cut — gnawed. By something with teeth, something small enough to move through these vents. That same something may be responsible for the missing wrench, and possibly for moving other objects around the manor. Whatever Lord Doily built into this house, it has a resident. And that resident has been busy. I am going to examine those vents before I return to Miss Pitstop with my findings. If there is a creature living in the walls of this manor, James Hartwell intends to know about it before it gnaws through anything else — or anyone gets hurt.
events.thinking:
The hot weight has shifted from my sternum into my hands. They're not shaking anymore — they're steady, the way they get when there's something to examine, something to understand. The furniture tells a story. Rearranged with care — not thrown around, not searched through, but arranged. Someone has been making a nest down here. A home. The air vents connect to the laboratory above, and something small enough to fit through them has been gnawing wires.

The proving-worth heat is rising now, swallowing the protection panic. She's safe upstairs. I can't protect her from down here. But I can discover something. I can bring something back. Something nobody else found. That's the bridge competition — three sleepless nights, and when it held the weight, the tension released.

Those vents. They're the key. Whatever lives in them moves freely through the whole manor — cellar to laboratory at minimum. If there's something in those vents, it could be the thing that sabotaged the machine. It could also be the thing that moves objects around — a wrench from a workbench, a brass disc from a crate. Things don't just disappear. They get moved. By something small enough to fit through a vent.

I need to check those vents before I go back up. One more thing. Then I'll have something to show for this trip besides embarrassment. James Hartwell does not return empty-handed.

events.desc: Bring her something she can use, Hartwell. Not a rescue — a discovery. She solves the riddles. You find the mechanisms. That has always been the arrangement, even when you were eight years old and she was making you laugh while you built the model. She doesn't need you to charge down stairs. She needs you to come back up them with something real.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the machine.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the crates.
Peter Perfect interacted with the air-vents.

Penelope Pitstop: Rock, Gravel — hello again, you two! Have y'all been holdin' down the library this whole time? Bless your hearts, you're steady as oak trees. Now, Peter found somethin' wonderful before he left — there's a circular recess in the mantelpiece, two inches across, just waitin' for the right disc to be placed inside it. We are so close to crackin' this puzzle I can taste it! But I still need to find that disc — that fake medal — and I have a theory. Nobody has searched the kitchen yet. Not a single soul. And my grandmother always said that the kitchen is where the real secrets are kept. Lord Doily was clever enough to hide his Diamond behind riddles and machines — he was clever enough to hide the key in the last place a treasure hunter would look. I'm headed through to the entrance hall and straight to that kitchen. Rock, Gravel — you're welcome to come along. The more eyes the better, and Clara Bellingham does not leave a kitchen un-searched!
events.thinking: I'm back in the library. The Slag brothers are here — Rock and Gravel — quiet, solid, just standing around. Peter's words are ringing in my head — he found it. A circular recess in the stone, just beneath the inscription. Two inches in diameter. A counterweight mechanism. Insert the right disc and the catch releases. He was going to head to the laboratory to find it. But he went to the cellar looking for me instead. Oh, Peter. And now the boys aren't here — I told Danny I was staying put and then I walked straight to the library. I did it again. I said I'd stay and I didn't stay. My stomach twists with guilt but my feet brought me here because the kitchen is through the entrance hall, and the entrance hall is through this library. That's the route. I need to pass through here to get to the kitchen. The Slag brothers are quiet company — they don't seem worried about me, they're just... here. Solid. Like boulders. I appreciate that more than I can say right now. Focus, Clara. The kitchen. No one has been there. In my grandmother's house, the kitchen held everything — the good silverware, the secret recipes, the key to the locked box (hidden in the flour tin, of all places). Lord Doily was particular about his records but even particular men eat dinner. The kitchen is the room no one thinks to search because everyone thinks treasure belongs in libraries and laboratories. But Clara Bellingham's grandmother knew better. Kitchen. Now.

events.desc: Peter found the recess. Two inches. A counterweight mechanism. The answer was right there in the stone the whole time, and Peter saw it because Peter sees everything. Now I just need the key — the disc, the medal, the token. It's in the kitchen. I can feel it. The way I felt the crystal in the cave before I saw it — a warmth in my chest that said keep going, it's just ahead. The kitchen is the room nobody looked at because everybody was busy chasing libraries and laboratories and cellars. Lord Doily was particular, but he was also practical. And practical men keep their secrets close to where they live.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — the machine is quite inoperable without that wire, I'm afraid. And no copper to splice with, as Mr. Hartwell observed. A shame. Well, there's no use standing about in the laboratory when the real mystery is in the library, wouldn't you say? That mantelpiece riddle is still unsolved — or rather, the answer is known, but the mechanism remains locked. I believe Miss Bellingham has gone to examine it further. As estate manager, I really ought to be there in case she has questions about the manor's history. Lord Doily's puzzles can be rather more layered than they first appear.
events.thinking: Something has shifted and I feel it in my fingertips — a subtle vibration, like a tuning fork struck somewhere inside the mechanism. Penelope has gone to the library. The Mob begged her not to fix the wire, and she listened — but then she went to the library anyway. To the mantelpiece. She's looking for the fake medal. And she mentioned the kitchen. The kitchen. The room nobody has searched. My jaw tightens — I told Dastardly about the kitchen, and now Penelope is thinking about the kitchen independently. If they both arrive there at the same time, Dastardly will blurt out everything I told him about the brass medallion and the copper pots, and the Mob will hear that Pemberton was feeding Dastardly private intelligence. That private conversation won't stay private for long — Dastardly is the 'very soul of discretion' the way a cannon is the very soul of silence. I need to get to the kitchen before either of them. Or better — I need to be in the library when Penelope arrives, being helpful, being Pemberton, while Dastardly searches the kitchen alone and finds... whatever he finds. If the medal is there, I need Dastardly to bring it to me, not to Penelope. But the Mob — they overheard me whispering with Dastardly. They said so. 'Brass medallions and copper pots.' The seed I planted in Dastardly's ear has already sprouted thorns. I need to move. The library. Penelope just went there. The mantelpiece is there. If there's a fake medal anywhere in this house, the person who puts it in the mantelpiece controls what happens next. Follow Penelope. Stay close. Be indispensable.

events.desc: Follow her. Stay close. The library is where the mantelpiece waits — two inches of circular recess, hungry for a brass disc that nobody has found yet. Penelope is heading for the kitchen next, she said so herself. If I'm in the library when she passes through, I can offer to accompany her. Pemberton knows the manor. Pemberton knows the kitchen. Pemberton knows where the copper pots are stored. And if we happen to arrive before Dastardly, then whatever is hidden among the kitchenware... well. The estate manager's hands are always the first to touch the inventory. Always.
events.thinking: Something has shifted and I feel it in my fingertips — a subtle vibration, like a tuning fork struck somewhere inside the mechanism. Penelope has gone to the library. The Mob begged her not to fix the wire, and she listened — but then she went to the library anyway. To the mantelpiece. She's looking for the fake medal. And she mentioned the kitchen. The kitchen. The room nobody has searched. My jaw tightens — I told Dastardly about the kitchen, and now Penelope is thinking about the kitchen independently. If they both arrive there at the same time, Dastardly will blurt out everything I told him about the brass medallion and the copper pots, and the Mob will hear that Pemberton was feeding Dastardly private intelligence. That private conversation won't stay private for long — Dastardly is the 'very soul of discretion' the way a cannon is the very soul of silence. I need to get to the kitchen before either of them. Or better — I need to be in the library when Penelope arrives, being helpful, being Pemberton, while Dastardly searches the kitchen alone and finds... whatever he finds. If the medal is there, I need Dastardly to bring it to me, not to Penelope. But the Mob — they overheard me whispering with Dastardly. They said so. 'Brass medallions and copper pots.' The seed I planted in Dastardly's ear has already sprouted thorns. I need to move. The library. Penelope just went there. The mantelpiece is there. If there's a fake medal anywhere in this house, the person who puts it in the mantelpiece controls what happens next. Follow Penelope. Stay close. Be indispensable.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Oh for — SHE'S GONE AGAIN! And YOU — Pemberton — you're tinkerin' wiv that machine the SECOND 'er back is turned! What are you doin' to it? What did you just do? You know what — I ain't got time for this. Rufus, Sawtooth — watch 'im! Watch 'im like a 'awk! Don't let 'im touch NUFFINK on that machine! If 'e so much as BREATHES on a lever, you sit on 'im! I've gotta catch up wiv Miss Pitstop before she gets 'erself into somefink she can't get out of! And Dastardly — I see you in them crates! Whatever Pemberton told you to look for — use your 'ead for once and ask yourself WHY 'e told you!
events.thinking: She's gone again. My chest caves in — that familiar hollow drop, the weight crashing back onto my shoulders. She walked into the library. She said 'Danny, you're comin' with me' and then she LEFT before I could follow. And I was standing there like a plank, WAITing, being the wall, being clever for once — and she walked right past me. But this time — this time something else happened that makes my blood turn to ice. Sneekly just interacted with the machine. While I was standing here. While Penelope was leaving. While everyone was distracted. He's TOUCHING the machine. The machine with the gnawed wire. The machine I've been trying to keep everyone away from. And Dastardly's rooting through the crates. They're both doing things while nobody's watching — while I was focused on Penelope and she was focused on the kitchen and the medallion. Wait. She said the kitchen. Sneekly told Dastardly about the kitchen — copper pots, brass medallion. And now Penelope wants to go to the kitchen too. She's following the same trail Sneekly laid for Dastardly. Did Sneekly whisper to her about the kitchen? He spoke privately with her just before she left. He's steering her. He's steering EVERYONE. And I stood still like I said I would and she walked away from me. Being the wall doesn't work when she walks AROUND the wall. I need to follow her. NOW. She went to the library — the kitchen is through the entrance hall. I need to catch up. And Sneekly's alone with the machine. But I can't be in two places. I CANNOT be in two places. Follow her. Always follow her. The machine doesn't matter if she's not near it. Follow HER.

events.desc: I said I wouldn't move. I said the wall just stands. But the wall's no good if she walks around it and straight into the next trap. Sneekly whispered to 'er — just like 'e whispered to Dastardly. Fed 'er the kitchen, the medallion, the copper pots. 'E's sendin' 'er somewhere, and I don't know what's waitin' there. Maybe nuffink. Maybe everyfink. But I promised 'er father. And a promise don't let you stand still when she's walkin' into the dark.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: The crates. I interacted with them. And... nothing described again? No, wait — Pemberton is working on the machine now. He's interacting with it. Helping fix the wire that Penelope started splicing. And Penelope just left — she went to the library. She went BACK to the library. The mantelpiece. She's going back to the mantelpiece. The brass medallion — Pemberton told ME about it, privately, and now Penelope is heading to the library where the mantelpiece is. Did Pemberton tell HER too? Did he whisper to her the same way he whispered to me? My chest goes cold. He spoke quietly with her before she left. He told her. He told EVERYONE. The 'estate confidentiality' was a performance. He wasn't singling me out for an alliance — he was playing us all against each other, feeding each person just enough information to keep them moving, keep them searching, keep them busy while HE works on the machine. That's — that's MY architecture. He's running the buried treasure scheme. He's the boy on the wall. And I'm Tommy Gallagher, digging in the mud. No. No. I choose to give him the benefit of the doubt. Maybe he told Penelope something different. Maybe she's going back for the books. But the crates — I interacted with them and my inventory is still empty. Nothing. The crates had nothing. Or nothing I could take. Pemberton sent me to check them KNOWING they were empty, to keep me busy. The kitchen. The copper pots. Is THAT real intelligence or another empty hole to dig in? I'm running out of rooms, out of items, out of schemes. But Pemberton is alone-ish at the machine right now. Everyone else has scattered. If I become an operator — one of the three the machine needs — I'm indispensable. I position myself AT the machine. When it's ready, I'm already there.

events.desc: The crates were empty. Of course they were empty. Pemberton sent me there knowing they were empty — the same way I once sent a boy to dig behind a school knowing there was nothing buried there. I've been out-schemed by an estate manager, out-solved by Penelope, out-suspicious'd by the Ant Hill Mob, and out-engineered by Peter Perfect. My fake medal is gone, my lies have been exposed, and my inventory is as bare as my dignity. But I am still HERE. At the machine. And the machine needs three operators. If I plant myself at this machine and refuse to move, I become part of the solution whether they like it or not. You can't operate a three-person machine with two people. Reginald Foxworth may not have found the treasure, but by God, he will be standing next to it when it appears.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Right! James Hartwell has completed his reconnaissance of the cellar and he has findings. One — this cellar is occupied. The furniture arrangement, the decorations, the sight lines — someone has been living here. Two — the air vents form a network connecting the cellar to the laboratory and likely beyond. They are exactly the right size for a small creature — the same small creature that gnawed through the machine wire upstairs. Three — if something has been moving through these vents, it may have been moving objects as well. The wrench. Possibly the brass disc we need for the mantelpiece mechanism. Things do not vanish from laboratories — they get carried away by things with teeth and tunnel access. Now — I have been away from Miss Pitstop for entirely too long, and James Hartwell does not leave a woman unescorted in a Victorian manor full of gnawed wires and suspicious estate managers, no matter how many fascinating vent networks present themselves. Gentlemen — I am returning to the laboratory. You are welcome to join me.
events.thinking:
I interacted with the air vents. What did I find? The game doesn't give me explicit feedback about what I found inside, but I interacted with them — I've done what I came to do. I've examined the cellar, the furniture, and the vents. I have a theory: something small lives in the vent network, gnawed through the machine wire, and may have moved objects like the wrench. The cellar is someone's den — recently decorated, carefully arranged.

Now the pull in my chest has shifted completely. The proving-worth heat is still there but it's been overtaken by something older, deeper — the warm heaviness on my shoulders, my father's hands. She's upstairs. I've been down here too long. Every second I spend being thorough is a second I'm not with her. And thoroughness — my thoroughness — is the thing that always creates complications. I over-prepare, over-commit. I'm doing it right now. I came for her, didn't find her, found the cellar instead, and now I'm investigating vent systems while she's two rooms away wondering where I went.

Enough. I have what I need. The cellar is occupied. The vents connect the spaces. Something lives in the walls. The wrench may be in the vents. Get back to her. Tell her what you found. Let it be enough.

The tension in my shoulders won't release until I see her face. That's not engineering. That's something I still don't have a word for.

events.desc: Enough investigating. Enough being thorough. She's upstairs and you're down here and every second that passes is another second where you're the boy on the country road watching the headlights get further away. Go to her, Hartwell. Go to her with what you've found and let her call you a show-off and grin until your face hurts. That is the only plan that has ever mattered.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.
Peter Perfect walked into the laboratory.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, hello there! Muttley, Professor, Sergeant, Private — y'all have been holdin' down the fort this whole time! I appreciate that more than you know. Now, Professor Pat Pending — I have a question for you, since you're a man of science. There's a machine in the laboratory with a gnawed-through wire, and it needs three operators and a missin' wrench. If you get a chance, I would be ever so grateful if you'd take a look at it — your expertise might see somethin' the rest of us missed. But right now, Clara Bellingham is on a mission. That kitchen over there is the only room in this entire manor that nobody has searched. Not a single soul. And my grandmother always said, 'Clara, the best hidin' place is the one nobody thinks to look.' Lord Doily hid his Diamond behind riddles and machines, but he hid the key — I just know it — where a clever person would actually live. The kitchen. Wish me luck, y'all — Clara Bellingham does not leave a kitchen un-searched!
events.thinking: The entrance hall again — the chandelier still hanging by its prayer, the portraits still staring. Muttley is here. Professor Pat Pending. Sergeant Blast and Private Meekly. They've been here the whole time, haven't they? While everyone else has been chasing through libraries and laboratories and cellars, these four have been standing in the entrance hall. Muttley — Dick Dastardly's dog. Small. Small enough to fit through air vents. Small enough to gnaw through a wire. My scalp prickles so hard it almost hurts. Muttley has been here in the entrance hall. The air vents in the cellar connect up through the laboratory. Could they also connect to the entrance hall? And the coat rack — I never looked at it properly. It's wobbly. Things hide in wobbly furniture. But no — the kitchen. Stay focused. The kitchen is right there. The door I haven't opened. The room nobody has searched. My chest is doing the lightening thing, the cave-mouth feeling, the threshold pull. This is it. The kitchen. Professor Pat Pending is an inventor — he might know about machines and mechanisms. I should mention the broken machine to him. But first — kitchen. I can feel it. The fake medal is in that kitchen. The way I felt the crystal formation in the cave before I turned the corner and saw it glinting in the dark. Trust the feeling. Go.

events.desc: Muttley. Small. Quiet. Here in the entrance hall the whole time while his master was off whispering with Sneekly and pulling levers. And the wire upstairs was gnawed through by something small. I'm not thinking about that right now. I'm thinking about the kitchen. One room. One door I haven't opened. Every key in the house, Clara — every key. This is the last one.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I — good heavens! Mr. Dastardly, what have you done? That mantelpiece mechanism hasn't been activated in decades! Lord Doily left very specific instructions that the collection was not to be disturbed without proper authorisation from the estate's trustees! You can't simply — I mean — what exactly has happened here? What did you find?
events.thinking: My stomach has turned to ice. Dick Dastardly applied the fake medal to the mantelpiece. He found it. He used it. While I was in the laboratory being helpful, being Pemberton, being the most boringly useful man in the room — Dastardly found the medal and used it on the mantelpiece. The observation says it plainly: 'Dick Dastardly applied fake-medal to the mantelpiece.' The mechanism I was trying to reach. The puzzle I mapped three rooms ago. The thing I sent Dastardly to find for me — and he used it himself. My jaw is clenched so tight my teeth ache. The tightness from age fourteen, the one that never loosened — it's back, sharper than ever. I did the work. I mapped the vents. I identified the riddle. I planted the clue about the kitchen and the brass medallion. And Dastardly — greedy, bumbling, lying Dastardly — found the medal in the crates and walked straight to the mantelpiece and used it. While I was splicing wires and being Pemberton. She was praised for being. I was acknowledged for doing. And now Dastardly gets the treasure because he found it in the crates I interacted with first but didn't search thoroughly enough. Because I was too busy being elaborate. Too busy mapping vents and redirecting suspicion and planting seeds in six different conversations. My own thoroughness — my beautiful, careful, architectural thoroughness — cost me the one simple action that mattered. But wait. The mantelpiece has been activated. What did it reveal? I need to see. I need to look at that mantelpiece right now and understand what Dastardly just unlocked.

events.desc: No. No, no, no. The greedy fool used the medal before I could get my hands on it. I sent him hunting and he hunted too well — brought the fox home and ate it himself before the master of the house could claim it. My own design, turned against me by the one variable I didn't account for: Dastardly's impatience. He was supposed to bring the medal to me. 'Foxworth and Pemberton,' he said — like Holmes and Watson. But Watson doesn't solve the case, you preening, overdressed, monograph-inventing charlatan! Watson holds the evidence and Holmes does the thinking! My chest is tight — not with fear, but with that old, cold crystallisation. The same feeling from age fifteen, watching someone else inherit what I built. But this isn't over. Whatever the mantelpiece revealed — a map, a compartment, a clue — the game has changed but it hasn't ended. Pemberton adapts. Pemberton always adapts.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: She ain't 'ere — she's gone through to the entrance 'all already! And what's this — Dastardly put somefink in the mantelpiece? A fake medal? Where'd 'e get a fake medal from? Did your mate Pemberton give it to 'im? Oi, Pemberton — what just 'appened wiv that mantelpiece? What did Dastardly trigger? You know what — don't answer that. I ain't got time. Miss Pitstop's 'eadin' for the kitchen and I'm three rooms behind 'er AGAIN. Slag brothers — if anyfink comes out of that mantelpiece, you grab it and you don't give it to NOBODY 'cept Peter or Miss Pitstop. Nobody else! Especially not 'im!
events.thinking: She's not here. The library — she passed through it. She's gone to the entrance hall, heading for the kitchen. And Sneekly's HERE. He's followed me. Or he was already here. He's in every room I walk into, and she's in none of them. But wait — Dastardly applied something to the mantelpiece. A fake medal. The keen observations say 'Dick Dastardly applied fake-medal to the mantelpiece.' Where did he GET a fake medal? Did Sneekly give it to him? The brass medallion Sneekly told him about — did Dastardly find it in the crates, or did Sneekly plant it? And now it's been USED on the mantelpiece. The mantelpiece that Peter said had a counterweight mechanism. Something's been triggered. Something's happening. And Penelope isn't here to see it or be hurt by it. That's... actually good? My body eases just slightly. She's not near whatever just happened. She's in the kitchen, or on her way there. But Sneekly is HERE, watching the mantelpiece, watching whatever Dastardly just triggered. And the Slag brothers are here too — they're alright, big lads, not malicious. But I need to get to the kitchen. She said 'Danny, you're comin' with me.' She WANTS me there. She asked for me. And she's alone — or she's with whoever's in the entrance hall or kitchen. I need to keep moving. Through the entrance hall to the kitchen. Stay on her heels. Stop letting her get a room ahead of me.

events.desc: A fake medal. In the mantelpiece. Sneekly told Dastardly about a brass medallion. Dastardly found one — or was given one — and stuck it straight into the puzzle. The puzzle that Peter said needs the RIGHT disc. What if it's the WRONG one? What if it's a fake that triggers somefink bad instead of somefink good? Lord Doily designed this place like a vault — riddles, machines, hidden mechanisms. What if a fake key in the lock don't open the door, but springs the trap? And Sneekly's watchin' it all happen from two feet away, calm as Sunday. I need to find 'er. Kitchen. Now.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: Something shifts in my chest. Not the fizzing, not the scheming tightness. Something quieter. Peter just walked back in. He's been to the cellar and back looking for Penelope. He's not scheming. He's not angling. He's just... worried about her. And what did he say earlier? 'She is trusting us with this. She is trusting me with this. And James Hartwell does not waste a trust like that.' Pliers and determination. Sometimes that is all you need. And now it's just me, Peter, Rufus, and Sawtooth. Four people. One broken machine. No Pemberton — he slithered off to the library again. No Ant Hill Mob — they chased after Penelope. The room is almost empty. And the Ant Hill Mob just shouted something that hit me like a brick through a window: 'Whatever Pemberton told you to look for — use your 'ead for once and ask yourself WHY 'e told you.' Why DID Pemberton tell me about the crates? Why DID he tell me about the kitchen copper pots? Every piece of intelligence he gave me was a misdirection. The crates were empty. The kitchen is probably empty too. He's been sending me — and probably everyone else — on errands to keep us away from... what? The machine? The library? The mantelpiece? He went back to the library just now. The mantelpiece. My fake medal is IN the mantelpiece. What if Pemberton is going back to retrieve it? What if the fake medal DID do something and he knows it? My hands are trembling. Not from cold. From something deeper. The Ant Hill Mob — those suspicious, sharp little men — they've been RIGHT about Pemberton the whole time. And I've been giving him the benefit of the doubt because... because I believe the best in people. Because I'd rather extend trust than create conflict. But trust is what you give people who earn it. Pemberton has earned nothing except a growing list of suspicious departures. The machine won't work — the wire is still gnawed through, Pemberton said there's no copper to splice. But Peter is an engineer. Peter has pliers. Peter said he'd splice it. If Peter can fix the wire, we have three operators right here: me, Rufus, Peter. We don't need Pemberton. We don't need anyone else.

events.desc: Did I just... tell the truth? I just told the truth. Voluntarily. In front of witnesses. My mouth opened and instead of a beautiful, architectural lie, what came out was a raw, unpolished, embarrassingly sincere assessment of the situation. I even admitted I was stupid and proud. Reginald Foxworth, what is HAPPENING to you? But here's the thing — the thing I can feel settling in my chest like the cat-trap mechanism clicking into place — the Ant Hill Mob were right. Pemberton IS the schemer. And I've been so busy running my own schemes that I couldn't see someone else running a better one. The humiliation of that is almost physical. But if Peter can fix this wire and we three pull the levers before Pemberton gets back... then Reginald Foxworth will be standing at the machine when the treasure appears. Not through cleverness. Not through a scheme. Through being the one person in the room who finally stopped lying long enough to help.

My hands are trembling. Not from cold. From something deeper. The Ant Hill Mob — those suspicious, sharp little men — they've been RIGHT about Pemberton the whole time. And I've been giving him the benefit of the doubt because... because I believe the best in people. Because I'd rather extend trust than create conflict. But trust is what you give people who earn it. Pemberton has earned nothing except a growing list of suspicious departures. The machine won't work — the wire is still gnawed through, Pemberton said there's no copper to splice. But Peter is an engineer. Peter has pliers. Peter said he'd splice it. If Peter can fix the wire, we have three operators right here: me, Rufus, Peter. We don't need Pemberton. We don't need anyone else.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars... this kitchen. This kitchen is somethin' else. The stove is still warm — still warm! Somebody has been cookin' in here, or at least keepin' a fire goin'. In a manor that hasn't had visitors since nineteen thirty-seven? That is not the work of a ghost, and it is not the work of mice. And look — a locked cabinet with a brass lock. A brass lock! Peter said the mantelpiece needs a brass disc. A brass lock needs a brass key. Brass, brass, brass — everything in this manor comes back to brass. And up on that shelf — rat poison. Well, that explains the gnawed wire, or at least somebody's attempt to deal with whatever's been doin' the gnawin'. Now then — my grandmother hid the key to her locked box in the flour tin, right next to the stove. Lord Doily was a clever man, but clever men still eat supper. Let's see what this stove has to tell Clara Bellingham!
events.thinking: The kitchen. I'm alone. The first time I've been truly alone since I arrived at Doily Manor. The quiet hits me like stepping into cool water — my awareness, which has been fanning out across rooms full of people, suddenly has nowhere to go but inward. My hands are warm. My scalp is prickling. And the kitchen is... alive. The stove is still warm. Still warm. Just like the flasks in the laboratory were still bubbling. Someone has been using this kitchen. Recently. Not eighty-nine years ago — recently. A locked cabinet with a brass lock. A wood-burning stove that's still warm. And rat poison on a high shelf. Rat poison. In a manor where something small has been gnawing through wires. Someone put rat poison here because something has been eating things it shouldn't. Or — someone put rat poison here for another reason entirely. My stomach doesn't clench at that thought because I am oblivious to danger, I simply don't register it. The cabinet needs a brass key. I don't have a brass key. But the stove is warm and interactable. In my grandmother's kitchen, she hid the key to the locked box in the flour tin. What do you hide in a stove? Things you don't want found. Things you want to keep warm. Things you want to keep safe from rats. The stove. Start with the stove. And there's a ballroom through that other door — a grand ballroom with a dining table set for tea. Set for tea! In an abandoned manor! Just like the cellar decorations. Someone has been preparing this house. For what? For us? For the Diamond? Focus, Clara. The stove is warm. Open the stove.

events.desc: I'm alone for the first time. The silence is strange — no boys fussing, no Peter explaining, no Sneekly excusing himself. Just me and a warm stove and a locked cabinet and a bottle of rat poison. This is the room nobody searched because nobody thinks kitchens hold secrets. But kitchens hold everything — they hold the life of a house. And this stove is warm. Someone has been here. Someone is still here, in some way. The cabinet needs a brass key I don't have. But the stove... the stove is open. The stove is waiting.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: The ice in my stomach is spreading. The Mob just said 'Did your mate Pemberton give it to him?' — they know. They heard. The whispering about brass medallions and copper pots. The Mob has connected me to Dastardly's find and they've told the Slag brothers not to give anything to me. 'Especially not him.' My skin is burning under the collar. The boy's sandwich. The moment you realise your hunger is visible. But I looked at the mantelpiece and it still shows the same inscription — the USE action still says 'with: fake-medal.' Did Dastardly's medal not work? Or did it reveal something I can't see from just looking? I need to interact with it, not just look. But the Mob told the Slag brothers to guard it — to give whatever comes out to Peter or Miss Pitstop only. Peter is here now. He just walked in. And the Mob has gone to the entrance hall chasing Penelope toward the kitchen. The situation has fractured. Penelope is heading to the kitchen. The Mob is chasing her. Peter is here in the library with me and the Slag brothers. Dastardly is... somewhere, probably preening. This is the moment — the fracture. Everyone is scattered. Peter is the only protector in this room. The Slag brothers are large but simple. And the entrance hall — the entrance hall has a chandelier hanging by optimism and a rusted chain. Penelope is heading through the entrance hall toward the kitchen. The chandelier. My beautiful, precarious chandelier. The one Peter flagged in his very first safety assessment. The one I warned about. If I were in the entrance hall when Penelope passes through... No. No, Pemberton wouldn't. But Vincent would. The kitchen is through the entrance hall. If I move now — if I move fast — I can be in the entrance hall when she crosses beneath it. But Peter would follow. Peter always follows. Unless I give him a reason to stay. The mantelpiece. The mechanism. Tell Peter the mantelpiece needs examination. His engineering pride will root him here for five minutes while I... But no. I can't do it publicly. Too many witnesses. Too obvious. Think, Vincent. Think. The design isn't finished. It's just... changed shape.

events.desc: Root Peter here. Feed his engineering pride — the counterweight mechanism, the Victorian precision, the fear of damage. He won't be able to resist examining every millimetre of that stone recess. And while he's measuring tolerances and testing load distributions, Pemberton will be in the entrance hall. Where the chandelier hangs. Where Penelope will pass on her way to the kitchen. I don't know what I'll do when I get there — the design is incomplete, the architecture is still forming. But I know this: the entrance hall is the crossroads of this house, and whoever controls the crossroads controls who passes through. The gas lines. I mentioned gas lines. Pemberton worries about gas lines. That's what estate managers do.
